v.q: Which test style should make up most of a healthy test suite?
o: Fast unit tests of plain classes
Tests that need a production database
v.w: The test pyramid: many fast unit tests, fewer slice and integration tests, and very few end-to-end tests.

v.q: Which test makes up the base of the testing pyramid?
v.w: Many fast unit tests, fewer integration tests and very few end-to-end tests.

o: Only the web layer, with services mocked
Nothing, it is just a marker annotation
v.w: It is a slice test. Provide collaborators with `@MockBean` (or `@MockitoBean` in newer Spring). Use `MockMvc` to call endpoints.

v.q: Which annotation loads the web layer only?
v.w: @WebMvcTest scans controllers and MVC infrastructure, and services are mocked with @MockBean.

v.q: What does `@DataJpaTest` set up by default?
o: Repositories and an in-memory database, rolled back after each test
The whole web stack, including filters and all of the controllers
A real production database that holds the live customer data
A Kafka broker that runs in a container for the test
v.w: For realistic behaviour against PostgreSQL or MySQL use Testcontainers instead of H2.

v.q: Which statement about @DataJpaTest is NOT true?
o: It starts the whole web layer
It can use an embedded database
It rolls back after each test
v.w: It loads only the persistence slice.

v.q: Why use Testcontainers for integration tests?
o: They run real dependencies such as a database in Docker
They let the tests run without needing Docker at all
They replace the unit tests so you no longer write any
They mock the database with a fake in-memory implementation
v.w: In-memory substitutes behave differently from production in SQL dialect, locking and types. Containers remove that gap.

v.q: Which tool starts a real PostgreSQL for a test?
v.w: It starts a throwaway container, so the test uses the real engine.

v.q: What is the difference between `@Mock` and `@Spy` in Mockito?
o: A mock replaces the object, a spy wraps a real one
A mock is for static methods, a spy for instance methods
v.w: Prefer plain mocks. Use a spy only when you need to keep most real behaviour while stubbing one method.

v.q: Which Mockito object calls real methods unless you stub them?
v.w: A spy wraps a real object. A mock has no behaviour until you set it.

o: It starts the full application context, so it is slower
It starts only the controller layer of the application
It runs all the tests in parallel automatically for you
It replaces the main class with a test configuration
v.w: Use it for a few end-to-end integration tests. Context caching reuses the same context between tests with the same configuration.

v.q: Which annotation starts the full application context?
v.w: It loads everything, so use it sparingly.

v.q: A test passes alone but fails when run with others. What is a likely cause?
o: Shared state such as static data, a shared database or time
The JVM that runs the tests is simply too fast for them
The name of the failing test is too long to be stored
The assertion library that the project happens to use
v.w: Tests should be independent and repeatable. Reset state, use unique data and control clocks.

o: Running tests in random time zones
v.w: Independent tests do not depend on order or on leftover state.

v.q: How should you test a method that depends on the current time?
o: Inject a `Clock` and use a fixed clock in the test
Change the system clock before the test
v.w: Injecting `java.time.Clock` makes time deterministic and avoids flaky tests around midnight or month ends.

v.q: Which statement about testing time-dependent code is NOT true?
o: A fixed clock gives repeatable results
v.w: Sleeping makes tests slow and still flaky.
